SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
S. D. REGISTRY
No. S. R. D. 8031
Date 7 8 37

The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Friday, August 6, 1937

Man Without Country
Due Back From Japan
Unless Japan showed more hospitality than this country Gustave Pick, German, was on board the Jean Laborde when that liner returned to this port this afternoon from Kobe. Pick, man without a country, after being released from a German concentration camp was allegedly deported to France where he picked up a criminal record. He then decided to go to Japan to start life anew, borrowing passage money and passport from Harry H. Dunham, an American citizen of Cincinnati, Ohio. He lost this passport on arrival here and while the Laborde was in port was passed from one Consulate to another, the French, American and German Consulates showing equal disinterest in the fate of Pick. He was finally sent back to the ship. If the vessel is still embarrassed with his presence, it probably means that Pick will return to France as an unwelcomed guest of the captain.

上海公共租界工部局警务处
特别股登记处
编号 S. R. D. 8031
日期 37年8月7日

《上海晚邮报与水星报》，1937年8月6日，星期五

无国籍之人
自日本返回
除非日本方面比本国表现出更多的待客之道，否则德国人古斯塔夫·皮克（Gustave Pick）将随“让·拉博德”号（Jean Laborde）邮轮于今日下午从神户返回本港。皮克是一名无国籍人士，据称在从德国集中营获释后被驱逐至法国，并在那里留下了犯罪记录。随后他决定前往日本开始新生活，并向俄亥俄州辛辛那提市的美国公民哈里·H·邓纳姆（Harry H. Dunham）借用了旅费和护照。他在抵达此处时丢失了该护照，而在“拉博德”号停泊港口期间，他被法国、美国和德国领事馆之间推来推去，这些领事馆对皮克的命运表现出同样的冷漠。他最终被送回船上。如果该船仍因他的存在而感到困扰，这可能意味着皮克将以船长不受欢迎的客人身份返回法国。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, THURSDAY, JULY 29, 1

Self-Professed Offender Has
Little Luck In Shanghai

American Authorities Seize Passport, Chinese Refuse
Jurisdiction Over Through Tourist

Gustav Pick, a young German, is a strange man in an odd predicament. He has tried hard to get arrested in Shanghai, but none of the authorities, Chinese or foreign, are interested in his case. So today he will be continuing to Kobe, where he may have better luck.

Pick is a third-passenger aboard the M.M. liner Jean Laborde from Marseilles to Kobe. He arrived here with the ship on Sunday and on Tuesday, for some unaccountable, reason, he confessed to the captain that he was travelling on another man's passport. He had an American passport while he was a German, he declared.

The passport was issued to Mr. Harry Dunham, of Cincinnati, Ohio, who evidently bears a striking resemblance to Pick. He said that Dunham had given him the passport in Marseilles and had also given him the money for his passage to Kobe. The passport had visas for France, England and Spain.

Notified, the American authorities took possession of the document, but were otherwise disinterested in its present holder. The man was then taken to the German Consulate, where he said that he was a Communist and had spent six months in a concentration camp in Germany. After his release he went to France, where he had been convicted six times on criminal charges. Even these confessions failed to move either the German or French Consular authorities to the point of action. Pick also produced a deportation order from France but to no effect.

Lastly, the Chinese immigration officials were notified of the unusual man, but they, too, were disinterested.

Earnest concentration on the part of River Police officials has failed to find a reason for Pick's confession. Evidently he wanted to stay in Shanghai, but why he did not choose the simple expedient of walking off the ship has baffled everyone.

37年7月29日

《字林西报》，星期四，193[7]年7月29日

自称罪犯者
在上海运气不佳

美方当局没收护照，中方拒绝
管辖过境游客

古斯塔夫·皮克（Gustav Pick），一名年轻的德国人，是一个处于奇特困境中的奇怪人物。他极力试图在上海被捕，但无论是中方还是外方当局，均对他的案件不感兴趣。因此，今天他将继续前往神户，在那里他可能会有更好的运气。

皮克是马赛开往神户的法国邮船公司（M.M.）“让·拉博德”号邮轮上的三等舱乘客。他于周日随船抵达此处，并于周二出于某种无法解释的原因，向船长承认他是持用他人的护照旅行。他声称自己是德国人，却持有美国护照。

该护照签发给俄亥俄州辛辛那提市的哈里·邓纳姆先生，此人与皮克显然长得极为相似。他说邓纳姆在马赛将护照交给了他，还资助了他前往神户的旅费。该护照上有法国、英国和西班牙的签证。

美方当局接到通知后接管了该文件，但对目前的持有人并无其他兴趣。随后该男子被带往德国领事馆，他在那里声称自己是一名共产主义者，并在德国的集中营里度过了六个月。获释后他去了法国，在那里曾六次因刑事指控被判有罪。即使这些供认也未能促使德国或法国领事当局采取任何行动。皮克还出示了法国的驱逐令，但未产生任何效果。

最后，中国移民官员也获悉了这名异常男子的情况，但他们同样不感兴趣。

水上警察官员们认真专注地调查，却未能找到皮克自首的原因。显然他想留在上海，但他为何不选择直接离船这一简单办法，这让所有人感到困惑。

THE CHINA PRESS, THURSDAY, JULY 29, 1937

German Exile With U.S. Passport
Here En Route To Japan

Gustave Pick, German, only a few months out of a Hitler concentration camp, became the subject of considerable diplomatic attention in Shanghai yesterday when it was brought to the attention of the authorities that he was traveling from Marseilles to Kobe aboard the Messageries Maritimes liner Jean Laborde on an American passport belonging to Harry H. Dunham, of Cincinnati.

The Jean Laborde arrived in Shanghai Sunday and Pick, who was traveling third-class, decided that he would rather stay in this city than journey on to Japan. He has a communist record and he was apprehensive of what might happen to him when he attempted to leave the ship at Kobe.

He remained aboard the French liner until Tuesday without mentioning his plans to any of his fellow passengers or to the officers. On the afternoon of that day, however, he went to the officers and explained his predicament, apparently hoping that they might be good fellows and let him debark without interference.

Consulates Informed

The officers, however, were not inclined to view matters in a passing light. Pick had confessed to them that he was traveling on a passport not his own and to them, it was serious business. They notified the French Consulate-General which in turned informed the American Consular authorities.

An investigation was immediately started and yesterday, Pick was brought before the German Consulate General where he made a general statement concerning himself and his activities. He declared that he had been lodged in a Hitler concentration camp for alleged participation in communistic affairs. He was held there for six months and then deported. He went to France, he said, where, during a short space of time, he earned a criminal record for himself. Six convictions were handed down against him, but according to his story, they were largely because he had been caught while engaging in communistic activities. The French finally decided to deport him and he produced a deportation order to prove that part of his story.

Says American Gave It To Him

He stated that he met Dunham in France and that they had become friendly. The American not only gave him the passport, Pick said, but also supplied the money for his passage to Kobe.

Pick pleaded with the authorities to allow him to remain in Shanghai but his entreaties were refused. He was told that if he persisted and tried to remain here, he could be prosecuted for traveling on a passport that did not belong to him. The American authorities insisted that the passport be handed over to them and Pick was accordingly relieved of the document.

When the Jean Laborde sails for Kobe this morning, Pick will be aboard. Just what will happen to him in Kobe is a matter of conjecture. Right now, he is a man without a country with no place to go and no place to land.

《大美晚报》，1937年7月29日，星期四

持美国护照的德国流亡者
在此途经前往日本

德国人古斯塔夫·皮克（Gustave Pick），刚从希特勒集中营出来仅几个月，昨日成为上海外交界关注的焦点，因为当局获悉他正持用属于辛辛那提市哈里·H·邓纳姆（Harry H. Dunham）的美国护照，乘坐法国邮船公司（Messageries Maritimes）的“让·拉博德”号邮轮从马赛前往神户。

“让·拉博德”号于周日抵达上海，乘坐三等舱的皮克决定宁愿留在这座城市，也不愿继续前往日本。他有共产主义背景，并担心在神户试图离船时会遭遇不测。

他一直留在该法国轮船上直到周二，未向任何同船乘客或船员提及他的计划。然而，当天下午，他去找船员解释了他的困境，显然是希望他们能行个方便，让他不受干扰地下船。

已通知各领事馆

然而，船员们并不倾向于轻视此事。皮克向他们承认他持用的不是自己的护照，对他们来说，这是严肃的事情。他们通知了法国总领事馆，后者随即通报了美国领事当局。

调查立即展开，昨日，皮克被带到德国总领事馆，他就自身及其活动作了总体陈述。他宣称因涉嫌参与共产主义活动而被关进希特勒集中营。他在那里被拘禁了六个月，随后被驱逐。他说他去了法国，在那里短时间内为自己积累了犯罪记录。对他作出了六项定罪判决，但据他所述，这 largely 是因为他在从事共产主义活动时被捕。法国人最终决定驱逐他，他还出示了驱逐令以证明其故事的这一部分。

称是美国人给予

他声称在法国遇到了邓纳姆，两人变得友好起来。皮克说，这位美国人不仅把护照给了他，还提供了他去神户的旅费。

皮克恳求当局允许他留在上海，但他的请求被拒绝。他被告知，如果他坚持试图留在这里，可能会因持用不属于他的护照旅行而被起诉。美方当局坚持要求移交护照，皮克随之交出了该文件。

当“让·拉博德”号今晨启航前往神户时，皮克将在船上。他在神户究竟会发生什么，纯属猜测。目前，他是一个无国籍之人，无处可去，无处落脚。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
Special Branch - C86.
REPORT
File No. 8031
Station 37
Date July 28, 1937.

Subject Gustaf PICK, German - activities of.

Made by and Forwarded by D.S. Pitts.

Arriving in Shanghai on July 26, 1937 on the Messageries
Maritimes m.v. "Jean Laborde" from Marseilles as a third-class
passenger was a German emigrant named Gustaf PICK. During
the voyage from Europe he was known on board as Harry H.
DUNHAM, American. PICK was in possession of American
passport No. 210474 issued in the name of Harry H. DUNHAM at
Washington D.C. on June 12, 1935 and renewed in New York in
the same name on July 7, 1937. At the passport examination
in Shanghai, PICK, who is unable to speak English, admitted
that the passport did not belong to him. Following enquiries
by the River Police and Chinese Passport Office authorities, XX
PICK was not permitted to land and will be returned to his
point of embarkation - Marseilles.

Questioned by the local German authorities at the
request of the River Police, PICK, a young man of 27 years,
stated that about 3½ years ago, he escaped to France after
having served six months in a concentration camp in Germany
for having participated in communistic activities. He was
the leader of a communistic youth group, according to his
own statement.. After the period of incarceration in the
concentration camp, he made his way across the French boun-
daries without a passport and did odd jobs to earn a living,
but for two years of his stay in France he was in prison
having been found guilty on charges of vagrancy and sodomy
In June of this year whilst in Paris PICK came into
contact with an American named DUNHAM, and both of them
being sexual perverts, indulged in acts of homosexuality
for three days and nights, after which DUNHAM, according to
PICK, 'out of the goodness of his heart' gave him (PICK)

日期 1937年7月28日。

主题 古斯塔夫·皮克（Gustaf PICK），德国人 - 活动情况。

制作及呈报人 D.S. Pitts。

1937年7月26日，一名名为古斯塔夫·皮克（Gustaf PICK）的德国移民作为三等舱乘客，乘坐法国邮船公司（Messageries Maritimes）的“让·拉博德”号机动船（m.v. "Jean Laborde"）从马赛抵达上海。在从欧洲航行期间，他在船上被称为美国人哈里·H·邓纳姆（Harry H. DUNHAM）。皮克持有美国护照第210474号，该护照于1935年6月12日在华盛顿特区以哈里·H·邓纳姆之名签发，并于1937年7月7日在纽约以同一姓名续期。在上海进行护照查验时，不懂英语的皮克承认该护照不属于他。经水上警察和中国护照办公室当局查询，XX 皮克未被准许登陆，并将被遣返至其登船地点——马赛。

应水上警察要求，当地德国当局对皮克进行了讯问。这位27岁的年轻人表示，大约三年半前，他因参与共产主义活动在德国集中营服刑六个月后逃往法国。据他自己陈述，他曾是一个共产主义青年团体的领导人。在集中营监禁期满后，他在没有护照的情况下穿越法国边境，靠打零工谋生，但在法国停留期间，他有两年时间在监狱中度过，原因是因流浪罪和鸡奸罪被判有罪。今年六月在巴黎时，皮克接触了一位名叫邓纳姆的美国人，两人均为性变态者，沉溺于同性恋行为达三天三夜，此后，据皮克称，邓纳姆“出于好心”给了他（皮克）

（印章：1937年7月29日）
（批注：lie / DSR / 29/7）
